measures.item: MG996R servo and its included horn/accessories
measures.what: Please measure body width, depth and height; mounting-tab overall span, tab thickness and mounting-hole center spacing (both directions); shaft center location relative to the body; and the horn's shape, mounting-hole spacing and included screw sizes. Tell me which horn and screws you have, and whether 'swing both ways' means ordinary limited clockwise/counterclockwise travel rather than continuous rotation.
measures.reply: servo body width: 19.82 mm (the case, side to side); servo body height: 40.4 mm (the case, top to bottom); servo tab holes: 4.58 mm (each mounting tab has two holes, open to the tab's end like a U); servo hole spacing: 44.61 mm (between the holes on the two tabs, from the inside edge of one to the inside edge of the other; I didn't measure the spacing between the two holes on one tab); servo tab thickness: 2.28 mm; servo spline: 5.84 mm (the output shaft, across its splines, where an arm would grip it; there's a smaller reading of 5.60 at the very top, and I'm not sure which feature that was); servo range: about 120 degrees, 60 each way (what the listing says; I haven't checked it); servo horns: four plastic horns came with it (a double arm, a six-arm star, a round disc and a cross), and I bought a 25-tooth aluminium single arm (the aluminium arm's hub is 14.66 across and 5.95 thick, the arm 3.86 thick, 34.62 from the hub's far edge to the tip, with 2.55 holes; I didn't measure where the holes are, or the plastic horns)

measures.what: For the mounting geometry, please orient the servo with shaft pointing UP. Measure: (1) case long horizontal dimension, short horizontal dimension, and vertical bottom-to-top height excluding shaft; (2) shaft center distance from the nearest short end and from a long side; (3) bottom-to-underside-of-mounting-tabs height, and top-of-case-to-top-of-seated-aluminium-horn height; (4) aluminium horn width at root and tip, shaft-center-to-tip length, and shaft-center-to-first/last small-hole centers; (5) bearing OD measured squarely across its full diameter, bore, and width. Does the aluminium horn have a split-clamp screw already installed, and can you seat and retain it securely with the accessories you already have? If a dimension can't be measured, please say so.
measures.reply: servo body length: 40.58 mm (the case, end to end, not counting the tabs); servo body width: 19.82 mm (the case, side to side); servo body height: 40.4 mm (the case, top to bottom); servo tab holes: 4.58 mm (each mounting tab has two holes, open to the tab's end like a U); servo hole spacing: 44.61 mm (between the holes on the two tabs, from the inside edge of one to the inside edge of the other; I didn't measure the spacing between the two holes on one tab); servo spline: 5.84 mm (the output shaft, across its splines, where an arm would grip it; there's a smaller reading of 5.60 at the very top, and I'm not sure which feature that was); servo horns: four plastic horns came with it (a double arm, a six-arm star, a round disc and a cross), and I bought a 25-tooth aluminium single arm (the aluminium arm's hub is 14.66 across and 5.95 thick, the arm 3.86 thick, 34.62 from the hub's far edge to the tip, with 2.55 holes; I didn't measure where the holes are, or the plastic horns)

measures.what: Please remeasure ONLY these essentials: bearing outside diameter (caliper jaws square), bore, width; aluminium horn's narrow arm width at root and tip; and whether you have the original screw that secures the horn to the servo. Can you also measure shaft-center distance from the nearest end of the 40.58 mm servo case? These were missing from the previous reply; say 'cannot measure' if unavailable.
measures.reply: servo body width: 19.82 mm (the case, side to side); servo hole spacing: 44.61 mm (between the holes on the two tabs, from the inside edge of one to the inside edge of the other; I didn't measure the spacing between the two holes on one tab); servo spline: 5.84 mm (the output shaft, across its splines, where an arm would grip it; there's a smaller reading of 5.60 at the very top, and I'm not sure which feature that was); servo horns: four plastic horns came with it (a double arm, a six-arm star, a round disc and a cross), and I bought a 25-tooth aluminium single arm (the aluminium arm's hub is 14.66 across and 5.95 thick, the arm 3.86 thick, 34.62 from the hub's far edge to the tip, with 2.55 holes; I didn't measure where the holes are, or the plastic horns)

limitations.wanted: A fabrication-ready servo-and-bearing joint using a properly retained stock servo horn.
limitations.blocked_by: The repeated measurement replies omit bearing remeasurement, shaft position, horn arm width, and horn-to-case clearances. No compatible servo horn-retaining screw is identified in the allowed hardware; the horn's 2.55 mm holes also do not accept the listed M3 screws.
limitations.why: These dimensions and retention details determine alignment and prevent the horn lifting off the spline. I will provide a measurement-gated design rather than guess a printed spline or claim the assembly is ready to run.
